name: Restate
title: Qoqi Flow vs Restate
tagline: Waiting for months is the point, not a smell.
lede: Restate replays a journal, so every side effect goes through ctx.run and the clock through ctx.date, by discipline. Running invocations stay on their deployment, and its docs advise against handlers that run for days. A Qoqi flow waits as long as the process takes, moves to new code at a stage, and the compiler checks the rules.

cards.title: Long waits are what flows do
cards.text: An approval, a trial, a renewal: weeks, months. Restate advises splitting such handlers. In Qoqi, wait time.after(90.days()) is one line.

cards.title: Nothing to wrap
cards.text: Forget a ctx.run in Restate and the call runs again on every replay, unrecorded. In Qoqi, a call outside a step does not compile.

cards.title: Apache 2.0, one binary
cards.text: Restate's server is under the BSL 1.1. Qoqi Flow is Apache 2.0, one binary on SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL.

code.title: Wait for an answer, or seven days
code.text: A durable promise, a timeout that throws, and a second handler to resolve it; or one wait match.

code.title: Plain code, because nothing replays
code.text: ctx.date, ctx.rand, ctx.run: Restate needs its own version of everything that changes between runs.

rows.label: How it comes back
rows.us: Its state thawed, at the line it was at

rows.label: A call outside a step
rows.them: Not journaled; runs again on replay

rows.label: Waiting for weeks or months
rows.them: Advised against: split into delayed calls

rows.label: New code under running work
rows.them: Stays on its deployment, kept up until it ends
rows.us: Instances move at a stage, checked against flow.lock

rows.label: A step that must never run twice
rows.them: ctx.run runs again if it was in progress
rows.us: Settled<T>: never run again; the flow is told Unknown and decides

rows.label: Crash testing
rows.us: everyCrash: the test again, stopped after every write, same ending required

rows.label: Steps in your own services
rows.them: An SDK in each service's language
rows.us: Any server that speaks the protocol: a signed HTTP POST. SDKs for Go, PHP, TypeScript

faq.q: Is Qoqi Flow ready for production?
faq.a: It is at v0.1.0. The language, the runtime and the daemon work end to end, and they are tested by crashing them on purpose after every write. What it does not have yet is years in production. Start with a flow that matters, not the one that holds the company up.
Workflow: impl Flow. ctx.run: step fn. Durable promise or awakeable: an Inbox field. ctx.sleep: wait time.after(...). orTimeout and RestatePromise.race: wait match. Deployments: stage.

faq.q: Do I have to rewrite my services in Qoqi?
faq.a: No. Only the flow is Qoqi. A step that needs your code stays in your service: any server that answers Qoqi's protocol, a signed HTTP POST. qoqi gen writes the typed interfaces for Go, PHP and TypeScript; any other language implements the protocol in a page of code.
Anywhere one binary runs. SQLite on one machine; PostgreSQL or MySQL when several daemons share the work. There is no managed cloud yet.
